ops.title: git sorts multi-ref push rejection lines by refname, so both token orders are reachable
ops.body:
Measured against real git 2.51 (2026-08-03) with a mixed push — one ref rejected
non-fast-forward, another declined by a hook — in one `git push origin a b`:

```
remote: policy: b is protected
remote: error: hook declined to update refs/heads/b
To /tmp/mixedpush/origin.git
 ! [rejected]        a -> a (fetch first)
 ! [remote rejected] b -> b (hook declined)
error: failed to push some refs to '/tmp/mixedpush/origin.git'
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not
```
exit 1, entirely on **stderr**.

**The per-ref status lines are sorted by REFNAME, not by rejection type.** Naming
the refs `m` (hook-declined) and `z` (non-FF) inverts the order:
`[remote rejected]` first, `(fetch first)` second. Both orders are reachable and
which one appears depends on branch names. Reversing the argv changes nothing —
`push origin a b` and `push origin b a` give byte-identical stderr, so caller
order is irrelevant.

**The trap this avoids:** any classifier that assumed "the non-fast-forward line
comes first," or that parsed only the first ` ! [` line, would be wrong for half
of all branch-name pairs. `gitPushRejected` uses `strings.Contains` over the
whole message and is therefore order-independent — correct, and worth not
"optimizing" into a line-oriented parse later.

Structure: git summarizes per ref (one ` ! [...]` line each) under a single
`To <remote>` header with one trailing `error: failed to push some refs`, and one
`hint:` block covering only the fast-forward case. A hook's own `remote:` lines
print BEFORE the `To` header.

Note on reproducing: use an `update` hook, which is per-ref by design. A
`pre-receive` variant yields the same token pair, but that does not demonstrate
selective declining — a non-fast-forward ref fails git's own fast-forward check
before hooks run, so it never reaches the hook at all.

See [ccx's push-rejection classifiers verified against real git 2.51 and jj 0.43]
for the per-arm verification.
